description: Build a Python module 'threat_feed_cache.py' that maintains a local cache of public threat intelligence feeds. This is foundational for Phase IV.a threat intelligence enrichment. The module pulls daily snapshots from: (1) URLhaus: https://urlhaus.abuse.ch/downloads/csv_recent/ -- CSV with columns id, dateadded, url, url_status, threat, tags, urlhaus_link, reporter. Extract the url column, parse out the hostname, store. (2) OpenPhish: https://openphish.com/feed.txt -- plain text, one URL per line. Extract hostname. (3) PhishTank snapshot: https://data.phishtank.com/data/online-valid.json -- JSON array, extract url field, parse hostname. Each fetched indicator is stored in threat_feed_cache table with columns feed_name, indicator (the hostname), indicator_type (always 'domain' for now), first_seen_in_feed, last_refreshed. On re-run, UPSERT so last_refreshed bumps but first_seen preserved. Module exposes: refresh_all_feeds() -> dict with per-feed counts; check_indicator(hostname) -> list of matching feed names; __main__ block that calls refresh_all_feeds() once and prints summary. This is a one-shot cache refresher -- a daemon wrapper invokes it daily. Do NOT include a polling loop.
context:
HARD RULES:

1. Use WriteService at http://127.0.0.1:8772 for all DB operations. Never connect to DuckDB directly.

2. For threat_feed_cache (NEW table): use /execute endpoint with explicit INSERT ON CONFLICT, NOT /write. Schema:

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS threat_feed_cache (
  id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
  feed_name VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  indicator VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  indicator_type VARCHAR DEFAULT 'domain',
  first_seen_in_feed TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  last_refreshed TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (feed_name, indicator)
);

id = int(hashlib.md5(f'{feed_name}:{indicator}'.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % (2**31) -- deterministic upsert.

3. Hostname extraction: given any URL, return just the hostname (lowercase, no port, no path). Use urllib.parse.urlparse. Skip URLs that don't parse cleanly.

4. Rate limits: these feeds are free but DO respect them. User-Agent 'zo-sentinel/1.0 (mcp-trust-intelligence)' + From 'hello@zocomputer.io'. Timeout 30s per fetch. On non-200, log warning and skip that feed -- don't crash the whole refresh.

5. Storage discipline: only store hostname, not full URLs. Do not store reporter names, PhishTank verifier names, or any other fields from these feeds -- PII concerns + ToS.

6. Expected cache size: URLhaus ~3000 recent entries, OpenPhish ~10000 active, PhishTank ~5000 verified. Total ~20k rows per refresh. Older entries naturally stale out -- rows with last_refreshed older than 30 days can be DELETED by a future janitor (not this module).

7. check_indicator(hostname) implementation: query threat_feed_cache WHERE indicator = ? AND last_refreshed > now() - INTERVAL '30 days'. Returns list of feed_name strings. Fast lookup, <50ms expected.

8. Logging: '%(asctime)s [threat_feed_cache] %(levelname)s: %(message)s' to stdout. Log: start of each feed fetch, HTTP status, rows parsed, rows upserted, total time.

9. One-shot execution: __main__ calls refresh_all_feeds() and prints {'urlhaus': N, 'openphish': N, 'phishtank': N} then exits. No sleep(), no while loop.

10. If a feed source is unreachable (DNS fail, connection refused), log ERROR and continue to next feed. Never abort the whole refresh on one feed's failure.
